problem:
Determine if $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$  is an eigenvector of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -6 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -6 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =5\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =5v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Av=5v,$ we conclude that $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda =5.$
